source.title: What Do Refusal Tokens Learn? Fine-Grained Representations and Evidence for Downstream Steering
source.authors: Rishab Alagharu; Ishneet Sukhvinder Singh; Anjali Batta; Jaelyn S. Liang; Shaibi Shamsudeen; Arnav Sheth; Kevin Zhu; Ashwinee Panda; Zhen Wu

record.tranche_reason: The study derives category-specific harmful-minus-benign activation vectors and adds them during inference, then measures refusal rates and general-task performance. This conceptually tests steering based on mean activation differences, but it does not test the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes from categorical steering and model-diffing measurements. The layer choice was empirical and preliminary; those selection results are not separately recorded. No results for ablation, weight editing, or jailbreak suppression are reported.
record.test_reason: The study builds sparse, category-specific harmful-minus-benign mean-difference vectors in a refusal-token fine-tuned Llama-3 8B. It adds them at layer 9 on the final token, with negative α on benign or ambiguous prompts and positive α on harmful ones, and reports refusal rates and capability scores. This is a different method aimed at V1's causal-direction question. It is not the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. The authors conclude that categorical refusal tokens induce sparsifiable, fine-grained residual-stream directions whose steering cuts over-refusal to near zero while keeping harmful-prompt refusal and general capability. They say model diffing proves these directions arise mainly from refusal-token fine-tuning. The authors call their own results preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: It computes harmful-category-minus-benign mean residual activations, but thresholds and sparsifies them into separate category vectors, then adds a selected vector at one layer and the final token during inference. It does not project a single direction out of all layers and positions. The study also compares base and refusal-token-fine-tuned models.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering is at post-MLP residual stream layer 9 and token position -1; vectors use threshold τ = 0.001 and top-K = 200 of 4096 features, with L2 normalization. Steering is selected categorically using an initially generated [REFUSE] or [RESPOND] token. The text states that positive α amplifies refusal on harmful prompts and negative α reduces refusal on benign and ambiguous prompts. Refusal measurement uses Gemini 2.5 Flash for the base model and generated refusal-token detection for the refusal-token fine-tuned and steered models.

fits_no_version.finding: Category-specific steering vectors computed the same way in base Llama-3 8B and the refusal-token FT model have low cosine similarity: 0.317-0.336 in four categories and 0.651 for Incomplete.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-token fine-tuning changes the mean-difference refusal directions relative to the base model, for most refusal categories.

record.problems: Refusal-rate results have no reported uncertainty estimates. The steering location was selected empirically from preliminary exploration and computational constraints. The intervention is category-specific and limited to one layer and final-token position, so it does not establish the all-layer, all-position effect in V1. For refusal rates, the paper uses different detection methods for the base model and refusal-token fine-tuned or steered models.

untested.parts: There is no single shared direction, no projection ablation across all layers and positions, and no induction of refusal on harmless prompts by addition. Only one refusal-token fine-tuned model is used, not standard chat models.
No jailbreak-mechanism analysis or adversarial training against ablation.
There is no comparison of a single direction with affine, cone or multi-direction accounts. The categories are mostly non-harm noncompliance types.
No cross-language or cross-variant transfer of a direction is tested.
Training is not varied, and the base model's direction is not tested causally; only cosine similarity is reported.

missing.what: Top features 4055 and 290 (also 682, 1039) recur across all five category vectors, while others are category-specific. This bears on whether one shared component underlies category directions.
missing.locator: Results 'Analysis on Category-Specific Steering Vectors'; Appendix A.3 Figure 4

record.verdict_notes: Caveats on the measurement: refusal for the steered model is detected by generated refusal tokens, but the steering vector is chosen from a token generated without steering. The text does not explain how the steered refusal token is regenerated, or how benign versus harmful prompts receive negative versus positive α. The base model is judged by Gemini, so cross-detector comparisons are invalid. α values and uncertainty for refusal rates are not reported. The harmful-prompt addition results (r16, r20, r24) are partial or absent, but they come from addition on already-harmful prompts rather than V1's harmless-prompt induction, so no V1 label is given for them. The steering site was chosen from preliminary exploration.

versions.untested_parts: No single shared direction is tested; no projection-out ablation at every layer and position; no test that adding the same direction makes harmless requests refused. Steering is sparse, category-specific, conditional, and applied at one layer and the final input token.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against ablation is tested.
The study tests category-specific vectors and reports their pairwise similarity qualitatively, but does not compare affine, cone, or dominant-direction-plus-others models.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representation is tested.
No cross-language or cross-variant transfer test is reported. Comparing base and refusal-token-fine-tuned models is not a transfer test.
The study compares base and refusal-token-fine-tuned representations, but does not vary how or when refusal training is conducted or test whether training creates a removable single direction.

relationships.condition: Negative-α category-vector steering on benign or ambiguous prompts, layer 9, final token, categorical refusal-token FT Llama-3 8B
relationships.reason: Subtracting the mean-difference vectors drives over-refusal to about 0 (r04, r08, r12). Capability scores are unchanged versus the unsteered FT model (r25-r27).
relationships.display_finding: Subtracting mean-difference vectors reduced over-refusal to approximately zero while capability scores remained unchanged relative to the unsteered fine-tuned model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: Refusal rates change under the study's conditional steering, and the reported general-task scores match the categorical fine-tuned reference, but the study does not test one shared direction or the claimed all-layer ablation and harmless-prompt addition; harmful-split outcomes also vary (r04, r08, r12, r16, r20, r24-r27).
